To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) self adaptive routing can achieve very good performance in dynamic environments, and (b) the performance of self adaptive routing is highly sensitive to the routing strategy used.

(1) user-optimal routing in dynamic environments can achieve very close performance to optimal, but it often comes at the risk of link overloads, and (2) optimizing dual objectives of average user latency and average link utilization can avoid the risk of link overload, but it comes at the cost that the optimal average latency can not be achieved.
